title: Support for .NET Framework 1.0 ends
impact: Apps still on the 1.0 runtime get no more fixes and need to move to a later framework

title: Extended support for Visual Studio .NET 2002 ends
impact: The Visual Studio .NET 2002 IDE gets no more fixes, so teams still building with it are on an unsupported toolchain unless they upgrade

title: Windows 7 becomes generally available
impact: Companies that skipped Vista start replacing XP clients, so desktop apps need testing under UAC and 64-bit Windows

title: Windows Server 2008 R2 becomes generally available
impact: It ships only in 64-bit, so server apps and drivers that depend on 32-bit-only components need checking before moving

title: Windows 7 becomes generally available with extended support scheduled to end in January 2020
impact: Client PCs moved to Windows 7 have a known end date, so the next client OS move can be planned

title: Windows Server 2008 R2 becomes generally available with extended support scheduled to end in January 2020
impact: Servers moved to 2008 R2 have a known end date, so the next server replacement can be planned
